Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1652. Arsenal targeting ‘prolific’ Serie A striker as Napoli and Benfica enter the picture

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Arsenal are reportedly among the clubs keeping a close eye on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, whose outstanding start to the season has attracted interest from several major European sides.

The 21-year-old Portuguese forward has emerged as one of Serie A’s most exciting attacking prospects, with his goalscoring form reportedly putting him on the radar of Arsenal, Napoli and former club Benfica.

According to ⁠Calciomercato.it, Napoli could look to make a move for Varela during the January transfer window as they assess their attacking options.

However, Arsenal are also among the clubs monitoring the striker, with the Premier League side representing a significant threat to Napoli’s plans. Benfica are another interested party after allowing Varela to leave for Monza last summer.

Varela has scored seven goals in eight Serie A appearances, placing him at the top of the league’s goalscoring standings at the time of the report. His performances have helped establish him as a player attracting attention beyond Italy.

The forward joined Monza from Benfica in the summer, and his immediate impact has made the transfer look increasingly valuable for the Italian club.

Although Benfica no longer have Varela under contract, they reportedly retained the right to match a future offer for the striker, alongside a 20 per cent share of any profit Monza makes from a subsequent sale.

That arrangement could complicate negotiations for Arsenal or Napoli, although it does not automatically mean Benfica will bring the player back to Portugal.

Monza also have little obvious incentive to sell midway through the season. Varela has become an important player for the club, and his continued scoring could strengthen their negotiating position ahead of future transfer windows.

Varela’s finishing record and strong start in Italy explain why clubs are beginning to take notice. Arsenal’s reported interest suggests he is one of the forwards being monitored, but there is no confirmation that the Gunners have made a formal offer.

Napoli could explore a January approach, while Benfica’s contractual rights give them a potential role in any future deal.

What this means for Arsenal: Varela is a name worth watching as the transfer window approaches, but any potential move will depend on Monza’s willingness to negotiate and the level of competition from Napoli and Benfica. For now, the interest remains reported rather than a confirmed transfer pursuit.

#1651. Mauricio Pochettino: Career, salary, tactics, clubs and trophies ahead of Man United appointment

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 12 Nov 2026 17:54

Manchester United are closing in on Mauricio Pochettino after sacking Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, having reportedly reached a verbal agreement in principle with the Argentine and prepared to pay to secure his release from the United States Soccer Federation.

Pochettino is currently head coach of the United States men's national team, a role he took up in September 2024 before signing a contract extension that will keep him in the position through the 2030 World Cup.

If confirmed, the move would see United become the seventh senior managerial job of the Argentine’s career, following spells at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States.

With that in mind, Sports Mole takes a look at Pochettino's managerial career, salary, tactics, trophies and top scorers, as well as why he left Tottenham and what United could expect.

Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol in January 2009, leaving by mutual consent in November 2012 before joining Southampton in January 2013 and moving to Tottenham on a five-year contract in May 2014.

The 54-year-old replaced Thomas Tuchel at PSG in January 2021 but left in July 2022, before taking charge of Chelsea in 2023 and departing by mutual consent in May 2024 following reported tensions over the club's direction and squad-building strategy.

Pochettino succeeded Gregg Berhalter as USMNT head coach after the 2024 Copa America, with the opportunity to lead the team at the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, forming a major part of the appeal.

Tottenham sacked Pochettino on 19 November 2019 with Spurs 14th in the Premier League after just three wins from their opening 12 games, barely six months after he had led them to the Champions League final.

Then-chairman Daniel Levy said the board was extremely reluctant but believed the decision was in the club’s best interests, following a League Cup defeat to Colchester United and a 7-2 home thrashing by Bayern Munich.

The problems dated back to the summer of 2018, when Spurs became the first Premier League side not to sign a player during a transfer window, and Pochettino had warned of a painful rebuild after the Madrid final.

The Argentine manager also admitted in Singapore that he would probably have left had Spurs won the Champions League.

Heavily influenced by Marcelo Bielsa, Pochettino favours a high-pressing, attacking style built around a preferred 4-2-3-1 formation, with his teams encouraged to build from the back and create chances through movement in the final third.

At Tottenham, that developed into a flexible system with advanced full-backs providing width, while Spurs recorded the lowest number of passes allowed per defensive action in the Premier League in both 2015-16 and 2016-17.

Pochettino has also shown tactical flexibility, using a 4-1-4-1 to beat Manchester City  in October 2016 and a more cautious mid-block during Tottenham's run to the 2018-19 Champions League final.

With the USMNT, he used a 4-2-3-1 in their 4-1 win over Paraguay at the 2026 World Cup, while also earning a reputation for developing young players such as Dele Alli and Eric Dier and giving academy graduates including Harry Winks and Josh Onomah opportunities in the first team.

Southampton finished eighth in 2013-14, their highest league finish since 2002-03, while Tottenham won no trophies under Pochettino, losing the 2015 League Cup final and 2019 Champions League showpiece but finishing second in 2016-17.

At Paris Saint-Germain, he won all three trophies of his managerial career, lifting the Trophee des Champions and Coupe de France in 2021 before claiming the Ligue 1 title in 2021-22.

Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24 and lost the League Cup final to Liverpool after extra time, meaning Pochettino’s only season at Stamford Bridge ended without silverware.

With the USMNT, he lost the 2025 Gold Cup final 2-1 to Mexico before topping Group D at the 2026 World Cup, only to suffer a 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last 16.

Southampton's Rickie Lambert and Jay Rodriguez each finished as the club's leading league scorer with 15 goals in 2012-13 and 2013-14 respectively, although Lambert's tally covered the full 2012-13 campaign, which began under Nigel Adkins, while Harry Kane scored 169 goals under Pochettino at Tottenham, representing 67.6% of the 250-goal club tally.

Kane won the Premier League Golden Boot in 2015-16 and 2016-17 and became the first Tottenham player to score at least 20 goals in five successive seasons during Pochettino's reign.

Kylian Mbappe top-scored for PSG in 2021-22 with 28 league goals, while Cole Palmer netted 22 times in the Premier League for Chelsea in 2023-24 to finish as the club's leading scorer.

Folarin Balogun led the USMNT scoring charts at the 2026 World Cup with three goals, including two against Paraguay, despite having his one-match suspension following a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina suspended by FIFA.

Pochettino reportedly earns around $6m (£4.5m) a year as USMNT head coach, making him the highest-paid coach in US Soccer history, and received $5.02m (£3.8m) during his first seven months in the role, including a $2.5m (£1.8m) bonus.

The Argentine’s salary at United is unconfirmed, but he could rank among the Premier League's best-paid managers, with a package potentially comparable to those of Xabi Alonso, Oliver Glasner and Enzo Maresca, whose reported annual salaries are between £10m and £11.5m.

United would reportedly need to trigger a release clause of around $10m, or approximately £7.4m, in his US Soccer contract, with further compensation required if the club also wants to bring members of his coaching staff to Old Trafford.

At Tottenham, Pochettino reportedly earned up to £8.5m a year and was linked with a severance payment estimated at around $16m following his dismissal in 2019. At PSG, he reportedly earned approximately €1.1m gross per month before agreeing a termination settlement worth around €10m for himself and his coaching staff combined in 2022.

Pochettino has long been admired by Manchester United, with the club previously considering him as a managerial candidate in 2016 and again in 2018, while Chelsea and Real Madrid were also linked with the Argentine at different points during his Tottenham reign. Spurs' final match at the old White Hart Lane in 2017 was a 2-1 win over United.

When United sacked Jose Mourinho in December 2018, Pochettino was among the leading candidates to replace him permanently, only for the job to initially go to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who started out as caretaker.

Fast forward to November 2026, and after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, ESPN reported Pochettino as United's favoured candidate, with Eddie Howe, Kieran McKenna and Julian Nagelsmann also among the names being considered as the hierarchy met Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

#1646. Manuel Akanji questions Cesc Fabregas's Como success after Inter win

By Naim Beneddra | 12 Nov 2026 17:57

Former Manchester City defender Manuel Akanji has questioned the excitement surrounding Cesc Fabregas's Como, insisting that the Italian club still have plenty to learn despite their impressive Champions League campaign.

Como have emerged as one of Europe's surprise packages this season, producing some remarkable results under the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder, including a stunning 9-1 victory over Lens in the Champions League.

However, their progress has not convinced Akanji, who helped Inter Milan secure a 2-0 victory over Fabregas's side at San Siro on Sunday.

The Switzerland international has now won all four matches he has personally played against Como, a record he believes offers a different perspective on the growing reputation of the ambitious Serie A club.

Speaking during Switzerland's international training camp on Wednesday, Akanji delivered a pointed assessment of Fabregas's team, although he also acknowledged the quality they have demonstrated since returning to Italy's top flight.

Asked about the so-called 'Como phenomenon', Akanji made little attempt to hide his scepticism.

"What phenomenon? I've played against them four times and won all four," the defender said during his international press conference, as reported by Tuttomercatoweb.

"To me, they're not that big of a phenomenon."

Akanji was referring to his personal record against Como, rather than suggesting that Inter had won every meeting between the clubs.

Indeed, the Nerazzurri were held to a goalless draw in the first leg of last season's Coppa Italia semi-final, a match in which Akanji did not feature.

The former City defender nevertheless recognised Como's progress under Fabregas, particularly their ability to compete in European football.

"Of course, they've adapted very well to Serie A and they also won 9-1 in the Champions League," he continued.

"They're a very strong team, but in the games I've played against them, they didn't seem superior to other teams.

His remarks followed another disappointing encounter with Inter for Fabregas, whose side arrived in Milan on a six-match winning streak across all competitions.

Como had attracted widespread attention with their extraordinary success against Lens in France, where Tasos Douvikas scored a hat-trick as the Italian club recorded one of the most emphatic victories of this season's Champions League league phase.

They had also defeated Manchester United 4-1 in Europe, further demonstrating their ability to trouble established opponents.

However, Inter proved a significantly more difficult challenge.

Goals from Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram inside the opening 20 minutes gave Cristian Chivu's side control of Sunday's contest, and Como were unable to produce a response.

The result extended Inter's impressive record against their regional rivals and ended Como's recent winning run.

Despite the sharp tone of Akanji's assessment, Fabregas had already acknowledged the difference between the two teams.

Before Sunday's encounter, the former Spain international described Inter as the strongest side in Italy and suggested that Como's development was still a work in progress.

Following the defeat, he offered another candid assessment of his team's shortcomings.

"We didn't start the game well, we made a few mistakes and we weren't confident," Fabregas told DAZN.

"We have to congratulate Inter, who played much better than us."

The Como manager highlighted the difficulty of competing against opponents with greater experience, particularly as his squad adjust to the demands of playing domestic and European matches every few days.

He also identified Inter's ability to exploit turnovers as a decisive factor in the defeat.

"They're very strong in transition, the strongest in Europe," Fabregas explained, acknowledging that mistakes in possession had left his players exposed.

His response was notably measured, with the 39-year-old refusing to search for excuses despite the disappointment of losing a significant league encounter.

Fabregas has transformed Como into an ambitious outfit capable of competing with some of Europe's established names, with young talents such as Nico Paz playing important roles in their development.

Their performances have raised expectations considerably, particularly after the historic victory over Lens.

However, Inter remain a difficult obstacle for the former Premier League midfielder, who has yet to record a victory against the Milan giants since becoming Como manager.

Akanji also acknowledged that Inter have experienced defensive problems of their own this season.

The Swiss international admitted that individual mistakes had contributed to several goals conceded by Chivu's team, but said internal discussions following their recent derby defeat to AC Milan had helped improve matters.

Inter responded with consecutive victories over Feyenoord and Como, scoring five goals without conceding.

For Fabregas, the challenge is to ensure that Sunday's setback does not interrupt his team's wider progress.

Como will resume their Champions League campaign against AEK Athens on November 24, when they will have another opportunity to demonstrate the qualities that have made them one of Europe's most talked-about emerging teams.

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 18:57, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 18:59

The top two in Group B4 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday evening, as Sweden welcome Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Both teams are bidding to secure first position in the section, which would mean automatic qualification to League A for the next Nations League.

Sweden have a record of three wins and one draw from their four matches in Group B4, which has left them top of the section on 10 points, two points ahead of second-placed Bosnia-Herzegovina with two games left to play.

As it stands, the Blue and Yellows will secure promotion to League A, but second spot in the group would lead to them dropping into the promotion playoffs.

Graham Potter's side opened their Group B4 campaign with back-to-back wins over Romania and Poland at the end of September, before drawing 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina in the reverse match between the two sides at the start of October.

Sweden will enter this match off the back of a win, though, beating Romania 1-0 last time out, and they are now preparing for their final two games against Bosnia-Herzegovina on Saturday and then Poland on November 17.

The Blue and Yellows are bidding to secure promotion to League A for just the second time, having previously competed at that level in 2020-21.

Bosnia-Herzegovina, meanwhile, will also have their eyes on first position and automatic promotion to League A, but they have work to do if that is to be the case.

Sergej Barbarez's side have a record of two wins and two draws from their four matches in the section, with eight points leaving them in second spot at this stage of proceedings.

As it stands, the Dragons are qualifying for the promotion playoffs, but they are only two points off leaders Sweden, so a win in this contest would be huge, while they are four points ahead of third-placed Poland at this stage of proceedings.

Bosnia-Herzegovina drew 0-0 with Poland in their section opener before recording a 4-2 victory over Romania in their second match at the end of September.

The Dragons then drew 1-1 with Sweden at the start of October, before recording a 1-0 victory over Poland in their last match.

Bosnia-Herzegovina form (all competitions):

Sweden are set to have their two star strikers in their starting side on Saturday, with Alexander Isak and Victor Gyokeres both in line to feature from the first whistle.

Dejan Kulusevski is back in the squad, having returned to fitness with Tottenham Hotspur this season, and the attacker could potentially be handed minutes off the bench.

Alexander Bernhardsson is in line to win his 19th cap, while Yasin Ayari could also potentially feature from the first whistle in this contest.

As for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Tarik Muharemovic is out of the match through suspension, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape for the contest.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored four times in 48 caps for his country, and the 28-year-old is expected to feature in the final third of the field, while there should also be another spot in the side for Haris Tabakovic.

Sead Kolasinac is in line to win his 74th cap for his country, but there is no Edin Dzeko in the squad, with the legendary forward recently announcing his international retirement.

Johansson; Beijmo, Smith, Lindelof, Gudmudsson; Ayari, Karlstrom; Bernhardsson, Nanasi; Gyokeres, Isak

Bosnia-Herzegovina possible starting lineup:

Zlomislic; Smajlovic, Katic, Dedic, Kolasinac; Memic, Gigovic, Basic, Mahmic; Demirovic, Tabakovic

For now, Arsenal’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing their attacking options rather than confirming a change is imminent. If Gyökeres’ situation develops and Tresoldi maintains his impressive form, the young striker could become one to watch in Arsenal’s future transfer plans.

#1637. PSG consider new Marquinhos contract despite defensive succession plans

By Naim Beneddra | 12 Nov 2026 19:18

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly considering offering Marquinhos a new contract, despite having already invested in younger defenders to prepare for the eventual departure of their long-serving captain.

The 32-year-old Brazilian, who joined PSG from Roma in 2013, is currently tied to the French champions until June 2028, when he will be approaching his 34th birthday.

However, according to Le Parisien, the club's hierarchy have raised the possibility of extending his stay beyond that date and have already discussed the matter with his representatives.

The discussions remain at a preliminary stage, with no formal offer reported and the defender's position on a potential extension yet to emerge.

The development is particularly interesting given PSG's efforts to build a younger defensive unit, including the recruitment of Illya Zabarnyi from Bournemouth and the emergence of Willian Pacho and Lucas Beraldo.

Rather than preparing for an imminent change of leadership, the French champions appear willing to consider keeping their most experienced defender for several more years.

Marquinhos remains one of the most influential figures in Luis Enrique's squad, having spent more than 13 years at the Parc des Princes.

The Brazil international has made 531 appearances for PSG, becoming the club's all-time appearance holder and playing a central role in their rise to the summit of European football.

He captained the Parisian side to their historic first Champions League triumph in 2025 and was again part of the team that successfully defended the trophy in 2026.

His longevity has been particularly remarkable considering the extensive changes to PSG's squad over the past decade.

The departures of several established stars have left Marquinhos as one of the few remaining links with the club's earlier era of major investment under Qatar Sports Investments.

His current contract was agreed in May 2023, when PSG announced a new deal running until 2028.

Although that agreement still has more than 18 months remaining, the French champions are reportedly examining whether another extension would be appropriate.

Le Parisien suggests that the initial discussions reflect the confidence PSG continue to place in their captain, both as a defender and as a senior figure within the dressing room.

However, there is no indication that the club have settled on the length or financial terms of a potential agreement.

The report also provides no confirmation that Marquinhos has decided to prolong his career in the French capital beyond his existing contract.

A new deal would nevertheless represent a significant commitment to a player who would be in his mid-thirties by the time any further extension approached its conclusion.

The possibility of retaining Marquinhos for longer comes at a time when PSG have already made substantial investments in the future of their defence.

Zabarnyi joined from Bournemouth in the summer of 2025 for approximately £53.6m, with the Ukraine international viewed as a potential long-term successor to the Brazilian captain.

However, the 24-year-old has struggled to establish himself consistently under Luis Enrique.

His first campaign in Paris failed to meet expectations, and his limited involvement during the opening months of the current season prompted speculation about his future.

The Ukrainian has nevertheless shown signs of improvement while deputising for the injured Marquinhos, leaving PSG with an important decision over his development.

The club also have Pacho, who signed a new contract until 2031 in September, alongside fellow centre-back Beraldo, whose agreement was extended to the same year.

Both players form part of the younger core PSG have assembled under Luis Enrique and sporting adviser Luis Campos.

Paris have continued monitoring emerging defensive talent, with Lens youngster Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou recently linked with the European champions.

However, the interest in younger defenders does not necessarily mean that Marquinhos would lose his place if he agreed to remain beyond 2028.

His experience and leadership could allow PSG to manage the transition more gradually, although the club have not publicly outlined such a plan.

The discussions surrounding Marquinhos also form part of a wider effort to secure the futures of several influential members of Luis Enrique's squad.

According to Le Parisien, negotiations with Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are progressing well, with the former potentially extending his contract until 2030 and the Georgian winger until 2032.

PSG have reportedly maintained their intentions regarding Kvaratskhelia despite the serious knee injury he sustained against Barcelona in October.

Talks are also underway with Desire Doue, while the club are working to retain promising academy players Quentin Ndjantou and David Boly.

Marquinhos's situation remains less advanced than those of Dembele and Kvaratskhelia, and no agreement is imminent.

Nevertheless, the decision to explore another contract for their captain suggests that PSG are not yet ready to put a definitive timetable on his eventual succession.

#1636. Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” said Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is important], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a big game in keeping that momentum.”

"We said at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not.  Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

The game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm)

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

#1635. Celtic 1 Kilmarnock 0: Liam Scales scores only goal as Premiership leaders make hard work of it

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EST, 8 November 2026

For Martin O’Neill, the second international break of the season should be somewhat less fretful than the first.

Seven weeks ago, with a home defeat to Ferencvaros coming in between two no-shows against Rangers, the veteran wondered aloud if it might be time to ‘wrap it up’.

O’Neill later admitted that he regretted his choice of words. He won’t, though, lament the decision to go again as he rests up in the coming days.

While the intervening weeks have often been a bumpy ride, the past four days have been a lot more like it.

Thursday’s dramatic win over Besiktas has breathed new life into Celtic’s Europa League campaign.

While by no means spectacular, this narrow victory over Kilmarnock re-established their four-point lead at the top of the Premiership and will have further dampened the sense of hysteria which was threatening to engulf the entire club.

Celtic defender Liam Scales loops the ball over Kilmarnock's goalkeeper and into the net

Scales celebrates with Camilo Duran after netting the only goal of the game at Celtic Park

Celtic striker Kasper Hogh finds the net with a crisp right-foot shot, only to have it disallowed

Celtic certainly made hard work of this. Truth be told, they should have gone into the break on the back of a far more convincing victory.

While they were right to feel wronged that Kasper Hogh saw his goalless run stretch to 16 matches after having one harshly disallowed, O’Neill’s men did not help themselves either.

Coming after Liam Scales had given them a half-time advantage, Benjamin Nygren’s missed penalty allowed Kilmarnock to keep believing right to the end.

Nonetheless, it was hard to begrudge Celtic their victory over the piece. A few weeks back, this might have been a contest in which they’d have come a cropper. They look more assured defensively than earlier in the season.

You don’t need to stay up all night researching exactly why Kilmarnock are in such peril at this stage of the season.

Neil McCann’s side began the campaign losing goals and they’ve really never stopped. They cough up more chances than any side in the top division. When it comes to shooting themselves in the foot, they’re in a league of their own.

In 13 games to date, they’ve shipped 29 goals and have kept just two clean sheets in the process. St Mirren, the side with the second worst record in the Premiership, have lost 22.

As worrying as those statistics and the Premiership table undoubtedly are, though, this felt like a step in the right direction.

In being more resolute, McCann’s men stayed in the contest right until the final whistle. They fashioned a number of decent chances throughout. There was plenty of encouragement here, even though they went down again.

For the home supporters, the much-needed positivity which had emanated from Thursday’s European win was boosted by the return to the starting line-up of Jota for the first time since April 2025.

Notably, only three out of nine of Celtic’s summer signings made the squad, with Sam Johnstone the only one involved who arrived on deadline day.

O’Neill was indebted to the on-loan Wolves man inside the first minute. Ieuan Owen skipped away from Callum McGregor then Colby Donovan down the left and put in a dangerous cross. Twice Tom Lowery hit the target. Twice the Celtic keeper stood up tall.

Lowery immediately had his name taken by John Beaton for a clumsy foul on Nygren.

Despite their precarious position, to their credit, Kilmarnock didn’t come to Parkhead just to defend. Tyreece John-Jules, their main striker, had an abundance of support in the form of Owen, Greg Kiltie and Joe Hugill.

Between them, they fashioned enough half chances. They just didn’t have ice in the veins at the right moments.

Hogh was right to feel aggrieved at the decision which cost him that elusive goal. Truthfully, there was very little in Mika Baur’s challenge on Kiltie which was retrospectively penalised.

Duran gathered and fed Nygren. The Swede swivelled and rolled the ball into Hogh’s path. A crisp right-foot finish was not that of a player lacking in confidence.

The Dane’s lengthy celebrations included a look up to the heavens. By the time Beaton made his way to the monitor and chalked the goal off, Hogh could have been forgiven for feeling that someone up there had it in for him.

To Hogh’s credit, he didn’t let it affect him. Moments later, after being played in by Duran, he was only denied his revenge by the outstretched leg of Nico Mantl.

Hogh then played Duran in with a clever back-heel. The Colombian lashed his effort just wide.

Celtic’s pressure was mounting and they edged in front on 26 minutes with Duran, yet again excellent throughout, the architect.

His clipped cross from the right caught the Kilmarnock defence flat-footed. Scales extended his left foot and watched the ball rise to the point where it appeared to be going over.

With Mantl hoping that it would clear his bar, it looped into the net. There was no disputing this one.

Required to take more risks, Killie had to be careful when they turned the ball over. Hugill and Cathal McCarthy were both booked for crude fouls on Duran and Jota, respectively.

While Celtic began to control the affair, the visitors were not without their moments. Michael Schjonning-Larsen’s stinging strike from 25 yards forced Johnstone into another solid stop.

While Jota looked good in moments, it’s clearly going to take some time before he’s fully up to speed. The same might apply to Hyun-jun Yang, the man who replaced him at the interval, after being sidelined for six weeks with a hamstring injury.

Donovan came close to wrapping up the three points with an enterprising run and shot with his left foot which flew just wide.

Duran’s close control and speed across the ground bought him a yard for a shot. Having seen it late, Mantl dealt with it well.

Hogh actually performed well here. He was tidy with the ball and frequently brought team-mates into play. He just didn’t hit the target often enough. That again cost him when he spun neatly in the box and tried his luck midway through the second period.

You couldn’t fault him when he seized on Kieran Tierney’s cross, though. The saving block from Killie substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara was tremendous.

With the home supporters longing for a clinching second goal, Duran dumped a shot into the side netting before the industrious Baur was flagged offside after firing home.

The wait would go on. Initially adjudged to have struck Aaron Tshibola’s arm just outside the box, Yang’s strike would earn Celtic a spot-kick with 14 minutes remaining after a VAR review.

Nygren just never looked confident as he spotted the ball. Mantl dived to his right and made a comfortable save. Those hoping for a sharp exit sat back in their seats.

The sight of Baur hobbling badly after being caught by Tshibola didn’t make the viewing in the final moments any easier. All that truly counted for the home fans, though, was that Celtic got over the line.

#1634. “Being talked about…”: Everton plotting January move for “interesting” England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1633. England vs. Croatia: Three Lions legend Harry Kane makes more history with landmark appearance

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 19:43, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 19:49

Harry Kane has officially broken the England men's appearance record, having been selected to start Thursday's UEFA Nations League clash with Croatia.

The Three Lions captain has pulled clear of the legendary Peter Shilton courtesy of his 126th cap in the League A Group 3 fixture at Wembley.

Kane drew level with Shilton against Czech Republic at the start of October but has now moved out on his own, setting a new record for the national team.

The Bayern Munich forward is comfortably England's all-time leading goalscorer with 93 and few would bet against him reaching a century of goals for the Three Lions before the end of his international career.

The 33-year-old made his England debut back in 2015, and this milestone comes shortly after he was crowned the Ballon d'Or winner, marking a remarkable period in his career.

“I don’t think it will ever leave me,” Kane told reporters when asked whether he continued to have points to prove in his career.

“It’s probably part of what makes me push myself to the limits that I do because in football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has.

“Whether it’s noise from the outside, from media or the fans … it just helps motivate me to realise there’s a lot more to achieve.

"My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more … if I could have just done that or done that.

"I want to make sure I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that whenever that day does come, I can say I’ve done everything possible. And I can sleep well at night.

“I’ll try to give them a good number to catch. The goal record, of course, is going to be one that’s difficult to beat for a while.

“I’ve spoken about leading by example and pushing a lot of these younger players. It’s by setting standards, being available every time, getting the caps and scoring the goals. That should help motivate the younger players.

"If I was younger and I had a player in front of me doing what I was doing, I know that would push me to think: ‘OK, I can score those goals, I can win the Ballon d’Or, I can break the cap record.’ Whilst I’m in this place, it is to try to set these records as high as I can and one day look back to see if anyone can catch them.”

Kane has pushed Shilton down to second spot in the all-time list, with Wayne Rooney (120) third and David Beckham (115) in fourth.

Kane has continued to find the back of the net at an impressive rate for Bayern this season, scoring 10 goals in 15 appearances, in addition to registering 10 assists.

Meanwhile, the striker netted six times in four matches for England during the last international break, which came in September and October.

Kane has struck braces in each of his last two appearances against Croatia and Czech Republic, and he will be hoping to add to his tally in England's two matches during this international period against Croatia and Spain.

#1627. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1625. Bonera believes Milan Futuro were not ready for first season: “Some thought it was easier”

Daniele Bonera has revisited his time as the head coach of Milan Futuro, revealing his belief that the team wasn’t ready to compete.

The Futuro project was launched ahead of the 2024-25 season to give Milan a ‘second team’ to allow their young talents to develop at a level above that of the Primavera league. They started in Serie C but were relegated in their first season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The decision was taken to sack Bonera as the head coach given the on-field issues, even though they were competing against experienced sides with a very young side. Massimo Oddo followed him, before the club chose to go with Sergio Navarro this summer, who has the Futuro in third.

Bonera was interviewed by Fanpage and he reflected on that period with the B-team and what he learned from it even despite the rough results, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“Milan Futuro was a great opportunity for growth. Perhaps we weren’t clear – and I’m part of this – about the level of Serie C. I had an idea of ​​it, but some thought it was easier,” he said.

“The squad had been built with expectations that were too high compared to what the league is. I don’t think that structure, at that time, was ready to tackle that type of league. On an individual level, however, I felt very comfortable. Starting at home was a positive thing.

“The biggest challenge was understanding which players you actually had available. Some were promoted to the first team, others were dropped, and still others were sent to the Primavera. We had guys who perhaps weren’t playing with us and then came back up.

“From an individual growth perspective, we worked very well in some situations. After a couple of years, we saw the individual value of guys like Camarda, Bartesaghi, Liberali, and Jimenez grow. The value of the players wasn’t in question.

“I think the problem was primarily structural: it’s not always the coach who’s the problem, but the way you do things and the direction you want to take.”
