The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1605. League of Nations: Italy-France, at what time and on which channel to watch the match?

France are the only undefeated team in the group, with three wins and one draw in four matches. It also displays the best defense of the four selections, conceding only two goals. The Blues won 1-0 in Turkey, then 1-0 in Belgium, before sharing the points 1-1 with Italy on October 2 at home, and winning 4-1 against the Belgians on the 4th day.

Italy follows with seven points. The Squadra Azzurra lost their first match 2-0 against Belgium, before recovering by winning 4-1 in Turkey, then bringing back this draw in France and beating the Turks 3-1. With eight goals, she has the best attack in the group.

In the event of a victory in Milan, France would secure first place before the last day, with Italy no longer able to exceed ten points. Belgium, third with six points, remains in the race and travels to Türkiye to open the day. Turkey, beaten four times and still without a point, brings up the rear with eleven goals conceded.

The Italy – France match, day 5 of the Nations League, is broadcast unencrypted on TF1 this Thursday, November 12, with an on-air broadcast at 8:35 p.m. for a kick-off at 8:45 p.m. which will be given at the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, in Milan. The channel extends its evening with the program L’après-match at 10:50 p.m. The other matches of the day are offered by the L’Équipe channel and its L’Équipe Live Foot platform. The Blues will return to Turkey on Sunday November 15 for the last day of the group, still on TF1.

#1604. Algeria vs Togo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 12 Nov 2026 21:57

Algeria host Togo at the Stade Hocine Ait Ahmed on Saturday, knowing that victory could strengthen their position at the top of Group I in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

The Desert Foxes lead the standings with four points from their opening two matches, one point ahead of the third-placed Sparrowhawks, who trail second-placed Zambia on goal difference, setting up an important double-header between the two nations.

Algeria have made a solid start under Brahim Hemdani, who remains unbeaten in his three matches in charge since September following Vladimir Petkovic's departure in August.

Petkovic's final game at the helm was a defeat to Switzerland in the World Cup round of 32, but Hemdani has since overseen a 3-1 victory over Zambia in the opening fixture of the AFCON qualifiers before his side recovered from two goals down to earn a 2-2 draw at Burundi on matchday two.

Algeria have now scored at least twice in three consecutive matches, including a 2-1 friendly victory over Niger in Tizi Ouzou in October, when Mohamed Belloumi and Ramy Bensebaini turned the game around after the North Africans conceded in the first half.

While that result extended the Desert Foxes’ impressive run, it also highlighted their recent defensive problems, having conceded 13 goals in their last seven matches across all competitions without keeping a clean sheet.

However, the hosts have kept Togo at bay in four of their last five meetings and won six of the most recent seven encounters between the sides across friendlies and competitive matches, which should give them confidence heading into Saturday's contest.

Togo are bidding to reach the AFCON finals for the first time since 2017 and made a winning start to their qualifying campaign by beating Burundi 1-0 in Lome, thanks to a goal from Dermane Karim.

However, Patrice Neveu's side failed to build on that success, suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Zambia on matchday two, which brought their six-match unbeaten run across all competitions to an end.

The defeat also marked the first time Togo had failed to score in six outings this year, since their goalless draw against South Africa in October 2025 during the final round of the World Cup qualifiers, where they finished fourth in Group B.

Currently 120th in the FIFA World Rankings, Les Eperviers face a difficult task against an Algeria side ranked 92 places higher, with Saturday's encounter also marking the first leg of a demanding double-header before the teams meet again in Lome three days later.

Togo also have a poor away record to overcome heading into this weekend’s clash, having managed just one victory in their last 13 matches outside their home country (D6, L6), dating back to a 2-1 friendly win over Niger in March 2024.

Algeria will be without Hull City winger Bachir Belloumi, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Brighton & Hove Albion defender Jaouen Hadjam and Hicham Boudaoui have also withdrawn through injury.

Amin ?hiakha and Rafik Belghali have also withdrawn from camp due to fitness issues, while Fahem Benaissa-Yahia has been called up to replace Hadjam and Adem Zorgane takes Boudaoui's place.

Yacine Titraoui has returned to the squad after missing the previous camp, while Mohamed Azzi and Abderrahmane Rebbach have received their first senior call-ups. Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri and Luca Zidane are among the notable omissions.

Togo will be without Sharani Zuberu and Steven Nador due to hamstring injuries, while Mansour Ouro-Tagba is also unavailable.

Lilian Brassier has received his first call-up and could make his debut, while Kennedy Boateng and Thibault Klidje have returned to the squad. Augustin Drakpe has also been recalled after recovering from injury.

#1603. GdS: Four exclusions, four defeats – Milan’s Pulisic dependance highlighted

There are many ways to outline Christian Pulisic’s importance to AC Milan, but one of them is very simple: wins.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have outlined the fact that when Pulisic starts a match, Milan do not lose. In an inconsistent team like Ruben Amorim’s, the four defeats this season to Benfica, Bournemouth, Bologna and Ferencvaros have two things in common.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The first is the two starters in midfield: four times out of four, the double pivot was Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari each time. Then, there are the three absentees: Mario Gila, Luka Modric and Pulisic.

Pulisic, Gila and Modric are clearly three of Milan’s key players, and the American arguably more so than the others. He’s eighth in Serie A in points average from starts (2.67 points, five wins in six games).

Pio Esposito, Lulli, Mora (the three who have always won as starters), Zaccagni, Dimarco, Isaksen, and Zielinski rank higher, but there’s a clear difference: the others play for Lazio, Inter, and Roma, the top three in the league.

Captain America came on against Benfica, Bologna, and Ferencvaros, and was an unused substitute against Bournemouth. Compared to Modric, who has been playing consistently since August, and Gila, who has been affected by injury, Pulisic has had his ups and downs.

He scored in Udine, the derby and most recently against Genoa, and it’s no coincidence that the Diavolo won all three games. Simply put: when Christian plays well, Milan follow him. When his level drops, Milan struggle.

It’s tactics, as well as numbers. Pulisic has different characteristics from his team-mates: he’s the only one who attacks the space in behind. Gonçalo Ramos often comes deep and lays it off, Alphadjo Cisse loves having the ball at his feet, and CP disrupts defences in other ways.

Furthermore, he’s considered one of the owners’ key players, who are also American, and he just renewed his contract. If you have to imagine the Milan of the future, just think Pulisic and 10 others.

#1602. Astonishing moment manager HEADBUTTS opposition player and is sent off, sparking mass brawl as FA Cup first round clash descends into chaos

By JAMES DUTTON, DEPUTY SPORTS NEWS EDITOR and WILL GOVE

Published: 16:39 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 16:41 EST, 8 November 2026

Oldham boss Micky Mellon was sent off for headbutting Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery as their FA Cup first round clash descended into a mass brawl at Boundary Park.

League Two Oldham pulled off a shock over their League One opponents, but the result was overshadowed by the altercation which occurred six minutes from the end of normal time.

The former Blackpool and Burnley midfielder appeared to grab Slattery by the back of the neck and pulled him closer to his face, before pushing his head into the rival player’s face and knocking him over.

The touchline soon descended into chaos with players and staff from both teams grappling with each other in a farcical melee.

Eventually the two warring sides were separated giving referee Martin Woods the opportunity to approach Mellon and present him with a thoroughly deserved red card.

Oldham, now with their manager in the stands, played on and incredibly nicked a 110th minute winner through Will Sutton.

Oldham Athletic manager Micky Mellon is shown a red card for moving his head towards Wednesday's Callum Slattery 🟥📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/5QMxgLt0dO

Oldham manager Micky Mellon was sent off for an astonishing headbutt on Sheffield Wednesday midfielder Callum Slattery

The scene soon descended into chaos as both players and staff from both sides entered the melee

Eventually Mellon was shown a red card and will serve a three match touchline ban

Wednesday piled on the pressure in the final minutes desperately trying to find an equaliser but to no avail as Oldham held on and advanced into the next round.

Mellon, however, will now have to serve a three-match touchline ban meaning he will miss his side's next appearance in this year's FA Cup.

Calum Kavanagh had put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross – his sixth goal of the season.

Wednesday equalised ten minutes later through former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Elsewhere in the FA Cup on Sunday, seventh-tier Wimborne Town stunned League Two Crawley 2-0 to reach the second round for the first time in their history.

The Dorset part-timers of the Southern League Premier Division South took the lead through Yang Seung-woo’s stunning strike after nine minutes, with Cameron Munn deflecting in Jackson King’s shot 11 minutes from time to seal the upset.

Stockport survived a scare to beat Cray Wanderers of the Isthmian League Premier Division 3-2.

The League One high-flyers were facing a shock exit when they fell two goals behind in the first half, a situation not helped by a red card for goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond for a foul outside the box.

From the free-kick, defender Alex Hernandez found the top corner to make it 2-0, but Stockport staged a late fightback, Kyle Wootton and, in added time, Mikael Mandron scoring to take the tie to extra time before Lewis Fiorini’s penalty won it.

Eighth-tier Stafford Rangers also led EFL opposition 2-0 before bowing out, Grimsby finding themselves facing an embarrassing exit against a team four divisions lower before hitting back to make it 3-3 after extra time, eventually going through on penalties.

#1601. Bundesliga: Leverkusen regains victory in Cologne

Bayer Leverkusen is smiling again! Traveling to Cologne this Sunday, on the 9th day of the Bundesliga, Carles Martínez Novell’s team won (2-1). First of all thanks to a brilliant inspiration from Aleix Garcia. The Spanish midfielder showed all his technical quality from the 7th minute of play. After a foul obtained by Patrik Schick near the area, the former Girona player took charge of the free kick and sent a marvelous strike over the wall, directly under the crossbar. A magnificent achievement which quickly allowed the visitors to take control of this Rhineland derby.

Behind this opening score, Leverkusen showed mastery to maintain their advantage until the final whistle and Patrik Schick even sealed his team’s victory at the end of the match. Despite a few attempts by Cologne to get back into the game, Carles Martínez Novell’s men displayed valuable defensive solidity to come away with the three points. Said El Mala’s goal in added time changed nothing. This success comes at the right time for the Werkself, who remained on three consecutive defeats in all competitions, against Hoffenheim, Stuttgart and Olympique de Marseille. An important victory to regain confidence, but also to relaunch a positive dynamic in the championship with a 5th place.

#1600. Wigan Athletic vs Barnsley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 12 Nov 2026 22:20

Two of the bottom four teams in the League One table will meet in an important contest at the Brick Community Stadium on Saturday, as Wigan Athletic welcome Barnsley.

The hosts have climbed off the foot of the division with a win and a draw in their last two games, while their visitors now sit 23rd and two points worse off.

Wigan Athletic return to action at the Brick Community Stadium aiming to continue an improvement in League One and a four-match unbeaten streak in all competitions.

They endured a dismal start to the 2026-27 season, picking up just seven points from their first 12 games having won just two and lost nine of those while scoring just eight goals and conceding 20.

That culminated in three straight defeats for the Latics in late October, falling to Oxford United, Huddersfield Town and Leicester City in three straight away games, before making a crucial return to winning ways at home to fellow strugglers Bromley with Christian Saydee, K'Marni Miller and Bradley Burrowes scoring in a hard-fought 3-2 triumph.

A goalless stalemate with Mansfield Town followed, before Gary Caldwell's side headed into consecutive cup games, beating Boreham Wood 3-0 away from home in the FA Cup last weekend and Crewe Alexandra 2-1 in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday with Jeremiah Chilokoa-Mullen and Rimmer Harrison scoring in the latter.

Now with some renewed confidence and their longest unbeaten streak since April, having moved within a point of escaping the bottom four while winning two and drawing one of their last three home league games, Wigan Athletic will look for another three-point haul on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, will hope to leapfrog their hosts on the back of a pair of cup wins of their own.

Back under the management of Daniel Stendel following a change over the summer, Barnsley have endured a similarly poor start to the League One season, now sitting ninth after 12 games with just nine points on the board, having managed two wins alongside seven defeats.

In those 12 outings, the Reds have conceded 22 goals and are winless in their last eight matches in the league, most recently hosting Oxford United on the back of four straight defeats and drawing 1-1, despite being reduced to 10 men inside 10 minutes, as they then led through Vimal Yoganathan and were pegged back.

A break in third-tier action then came in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy, firstly thrashing Aldershot 7-2 to advance in the former before beating Oldham Athletic 5-2 on Wednesday with Makenzie Kirk scoring a brace alongside goals from Daniel Johnson, Yoganathan and Luke Alker.

Having rebuilt crucial optimism with a pair of convincing cup wins, on the back of an improved display against Oxford, Barnsley will now bid to make it three straight wins and a first league victory since early September to boost their own standing at the bottom end of the table.

Wigan Athletic will likely be without forward Scott Hogan, who picked up an injury against Mansfield and missed their two cup games, while Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris should also miss out.

Those absences leave the Latics light up top, and Reggie Walsh and Bradley Burrowes may support lone front man Christian Saydee.

Fraser Murray started in both cup games having returned from a suspension off the bench against Mansfield and could start at the weekend, while Charlie Gray and Jon Mellish will likely compete to join Max Power in midfield.

Barnsley remain without defender Connor O'Riordan and attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo through injury.

Key midfielder Patrick Kelly is also away on international duty with Northern Ireland, meaning Daniel Johnson should partner Luca Connell in the engine room after his midweek goal.

Ahead of them, Makenzie Kirk, who got a brace on Tuesday, should get the nod to lead the line with support from Yoganathan, Cameron McGeehan and Reyes Cleary.

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Weir; Barrett, Power, Gray, Murray; Walsh, Saydee, Burrowes

Slicker; Noslin, Kay, Shepherd, Larkeche; Johnson, Connell; Yoganathan, McGeehan, Cleary; Kirk

Both teams have shown signs of improvement in recent weeks and will be desperate to avoid a defeat which would halt their progress and keep them in the drop zone while again draining their confidence.

For that reason, we can envisage the contest ending level at the Brick Community Stadium as both push to continue unbeaten streaks.

#1598. Man United transfer news: £40m striker 'actively' exploring move to become Mauricio Pochettino's first signing in January

By Lewis Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 23:15

Mauricio Pochettino's impending appointment as Manchester United boss has made Old Trafford a more appealing destination for Folarin Balogun, the latest report has claimed

In news that most had long expected, Michael Carrick was dismissed from his role as head coach of the Red Devils on Thursday.

Fans may not have to wait long for official confirmation of his successor given USA manager Pochettino is said to be closing in on a move to the club.

United are 18th in the Premier League, so the incoming boss will almost certainly look to make additions in the January transfer window.

A new TEAMtalk report claims that US striker Balogun and his camp are actively exploring the a switch from Monaco to Old Trafford.

Balogun was one of the standout stars of the US national team at the 2026 World Cup, scoring three goals, though his tournament was ultimately overshadowed by FIFA controversially overturning his red card.

The 25-year-old has only scored one goal for Monaco this season, but he has only played 233 minutes in all competitions after a disrupted summer following his failed move to Everton.

Pochettino is already familiar with the forward's ability to press and make runs in behind defences, and a haul of 46 goals and 11 assists in 115 Ligue 1 games is impressive.

Balogun nearly made the switch from Monaco to Everton for £40m in the summer, and if United could sign him for a similar fee, he could be a sensible addition as an immediate starter before becoming a long-term member of their squad.

Pochettino's best teams have all been energetic, but there are a number of players in the current United squad that may struggle with such an aggressive system.

Replacing Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez in one window will almost certainly not be possible, but a new defender must be seen as a priority.

The Red Devils already have younger centre-backs Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro at the club, so perhaps they should focus their efforts on signing a senior and reliable partner for them.

#1597. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

The players are lining up around the centre circle, with a minute of silence for the victims of the tragedy in Nepal.

I wrote a little while ago that it was an unpleasantly warm evening in Naples. I now want to revise that comment. It’s nastily hot, and it’s getting worse. The air is thick (27 degrees and 74 per cent humidity, according to my weather app) and I can’t imagine it will be easy for the players.

As the players line up in the tunnel, here are the full teams in black and white:

Subs: Kepa, Meslier, Tzolis, Madueke, Havertz, Calafiori, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman, Salmon

Liverpool vs Atlético Madrid – join Kieran on our live blog here

First goal for Barcelona 📞Gabriel Jesus bags Barcelona's fifth 🇧🇷 📺 Watch on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/TJmIhMkoXo

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a new leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

#1595. Northern Ireland vs Ukraine - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 23:59

Fighting to maintain their lead at the top UEFA Nations League B's Group 2, Northern Ireland will host Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday.

The Norn Iron are unbeaten in the competition so far, while the Blue and Yellow arrive on the back of a three-game winless run.

Michael O'Neill's Northern Ireland are pushing for promotion to League A this term, after delivering a strong showing across their four Nations League clashes to date.

The Norn Iron have yet to concede a goal in Group 2, and currently sit at the top of the pile with eight points.

However, O'Neill's side are just one point above second-placed Hungary, who will be expecting to beat struggling Georgia on matchday five.

With that in mind, Northern Ireland will likely need to triumph this weekend in order to keep their automatic promotion spot, but for all their defensive resilience, they have found goals hard to come by.

Saturday's hosts played out a goalless draw with Georgia at on October 5, meaning that they have failed to find the back of the net at Windsor Park in this iteration of the Nations League, after a 0-0 stalemate with Hungary in late September.

On a more positive note, O'Neill's men thoroughly beat Ukraine 3-0 at City Arena Trnava last month - courtesy of a surprise brace from Ciaron Brown either side of a header from Isaac Price - a result that could give the Norn Iron a psychological edge.

Meanwhile, Andrea Maldera's Ukraine are at risk of relegation from League B after their campaign turned sour in October.

The Blue and Yellow kicked off with a commendable 1-0 victory over Hungary on September 25 before a 0-0 draw with Georgia three days later.

However, Maldera's side have not collected a single point since, following their 3-0 beating by Northern Ireland with a 2-1 defeat to Hungary most recently.

As a result, Ukraine are now third in Group 2 with just four points to their name, three behind second-placed Hungary and four short of the leaders.

A late promotion push seems unlikely, and with Georgia sitting just two points off the Blue and Yellow in the automatic relegation spot, the visitors will be focused on avoiding the drop.

Supporters searching for a positive could lean on the fact Ukraine are unbeaten on the road in the Nations League this term, though Maldera's men have only netted twice in four group games.

Northern Ireland are lighter in defence than ideal without Sunderland centre-back Dan Ballard (hamstring), Bolton Wanderers' Eoin Toal (muscle), or captain and Liverpool right-back Conor Bradley (knee).

In their absence, O'Neill could opt for a three-man line of Tom Atcheson, Ruairi McConville and Ciaron Brown in front of goalkeeper Pierce Charles, with Trai Hume and Justin Devenny as wing-backs.

As for Ukraine, they are missing Ajax duo Viktor Tsygankov and Oleksandr Zinchenko (knee), formerly of Manchester City and Arsenal, through injury.

With that in mind, expect to see Yehor Nazaryna and Georgiy Sudakov operate out wide, either side of Oleh Ocheretko and Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk in midfield.

Just behind them is likely to be a four-man defence featuring Paris Saint-Germain's Ilya Zabarnyi and Shakhtar Donetsk's Mykola Matvienko at centre-half, as well as Illia Krupskyi and Everton star Vitaliy Mykolenko at full-back.

Northern Ireland possible starting lineup:

P Charles; Atcheson, McConville, Brown; Hume, S Charles, Galbraith, Devenny; Kelly, Price; Donley

Trubin; Krupskyi, Zabarnyi, Matvienko, Mykolenko; Nazaryna, Ocheretko, Yarmoliuk, Sudakov; Yarmechuk, Sikan

Northern Ireland have been far from free flowing in the Nations League, but their defensive resilience has been impressive, especially with the likes of Ballard sidelined.

Ukraine have struggled even more than their hosts up front, and could find the Norn Iron's backline a tough test.

#1594. HEARTS 2 FALKIRK 5: Wouter Vrancken slams 'childish' Hearts as five-star Bairns toy with injury-hit capital men at Tynecastle

Published: 16:57 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:00 EST, 8 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken condemned a ‘ridiculous’ first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Tynecastle side, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a fifth Premiership win in a row.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Gorgie men, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

‘This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,’ said Vrancken. ‘Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

‘When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

American striker Jacob Murrell races off to celebrate his side's fifth goal on a day to remember

‘It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody — me, staff, players — have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.’

To exacerbate their grim predicament, Hearts lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

‘This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,’ said Vrancken. ‘Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who was good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.’

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who secured five consecutive top-flight victories for the first time in 31 years.

‘I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,’ said Bairns manager John McGlynn. ‘First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

‘We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. Hearts had a lot of the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it.’

Wouter Vrancken has been beset by injury concerns but he was in no mood for excuses

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Yan Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

Within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Former Hearts boss John McGlynn led his side to a quite remarkable fifth consecutive win

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute. Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was far too little, far too late.

McGlynn added: ‘We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. Our play was outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

‘Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.’

#1591. Mauricio Pochettino contract 'agreed': Details revealed as major problem emerges before first game against Liverpool

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 00:28

Mauricio Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year deal to become the next Manchester United manager, the newest report has revealed.

After leaving the Red Devils 18th in the Premier League table with just eight points from their first 10 matches, it came as no surprise to anyone to see the club sack Michael Carrick on Thursday.

He became the seventh permanent manager to lose his job since the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, and fans will hope that the next boss can be the one to finally bring the team back to the pinnacle of English football.

Pochettino was widely reported to be the frontrunner, even ahead of candidates like Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Athletic have revealed that the Argentine is set to sign a contract until 2029, and his first game will come against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

A win at Anfield against Liverpool would be the best possible start to life as United boss for Pochettino, but there are concerns about how long he will have to prepare for that match.

The 54-year-old is expected to take charge of the USA national team for the country's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final legs against Haiti.

Those clashes will take place on Saturday and on Wednesday, while the Red Devils will face Liverpool on Sunday, meaning he will have very little time to prepare his squad for their clash against their biggest rivals.

Many thought that Carrick would be dismissed weeks ago, so the fact that United have waited until now to agree a deal with Pochettino is yet another indictment on the chaos behind the scenes at Old Trafford.

Pochettino will need grace given United are arguably at their lowest ever period since Ferguson's retirement, but fans should be excited about the club's next manager.

The 54-year-old's Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton sides were some of the hardest working teams in Europe, and that type of intensity has long been missing at Old Trafford.

If Pochettino can change the culture in training and in the squad, that could have a lasting effect beyond his tenure in Manchester.

The only question is whether the Argentine will be backed sufficiently by the decision makers above him, as if he is let down by the likes of Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, then United's ceiling under him will be capped.

#1590. Romania vs Poland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 13 Nov 2026 01:20

Romania and Poland will lock horns at the Arena Nationala in Bucharest on Saturday night, with both nations desperate to get their UEFA Nations League campaigns back on track.

Pressure is mounting on both managers, while the threat of relegation from League B adds further intrigue to an already tasty contest.

When Gheorghe Hagi returned to take charge of the Romanian national team last April, he brought with him a wave of optimism, although that feel-good factor has proved remarkably short-lived.

Less than six months into his reign, the Tricolours find themselves in the middle of a full-blown meltdown, with problems extending well beyond their disappointing results on the pitch.

Hagi initially took aim at the Romanian media ahead of the Nations League campaign, accusing journalists of being overly pessimistic before boldly predicting that his side would collect all 12 points from their opening four matches.

Reality has been less kind, with Romania losing all four encounters while shipping 13 goals in the process.

Putting aside the on-field problems, there have been a series of bitter public exchanges between Hagi and high-profile members of the Romanian national team - especially in the last few days.

Nicolae Stanciu, for example, was accused by Hagi during the pre-match press conference of snubbing the national team - a claim that prompted the midfielder to hit back on Instagram with screenshots of his medical diagnosis and an X-ray of his injured leg.

Ionut Radu also found himself in Hagi's firing line, with the Celta Vigo goalkeeper responding to a similar accusation with a Cristiano Ronaldo-esque 800-word Instagram statement, where he explained that he had been struggling with a shoulder problem for several months.

If the public fallout with his players was not enough, Hagi is also facing accusations of nepotism, with Romanian journalists questioning whether his son, Ianis, has earned his place in the squad on merit.

The 28-year-old has struggled for form at Turkish side Alanyaspor, registering just one assist in 11 appearances this season while spending the entirety of last weekend's game on the substitutes' bench.

With two games remaining, Poland hold a four-point cushion over bottom-placed Romania, meaning a draw on Saturday would be enough to guarantee their League B status.

The Poles will be encouraged by the fact they beat Romania 6-0 during the last international break, although that was just one of two victories Jan Urban's side have recorded in 2026.

Failing to qualify for last summer’s World Cup was a bitter disappointment for the Polish national side, though their subsequent results have left Urban clinging on to his role.

Defeats to Sweden and Bosnia & Herzegovina during the previous international break have ramped up the pressure on the current manager, with the Polish football federation set to make a decision on his future after the next two matches.

Saturday's trip to Bucharest presents a potentially tricky assignment, particularly given that Poland have recorded just two away victories in the last 24 months, both against relatively low-ranked opposition in Malta and Lithuania.

Six defeats in their last nine away matches and just one clean sheet across their previous 10 hardly make for encouraging reading, suggesting Urban's men could have a difficult evening ahead.

As previously mentioned, Romania will be without captain Stanciu and goalkeeper Radu following their injury troubles.

Razvan Marin is also unavailable as the 30-year-old serves his suspension.

In-form Alexandru Cicaldau scored against Bosnia in the previous international break, and the midfielder has since performed well for his club Universitatea Craiova.

Striker Daniel Birligea is expected to lead the attack, having scored two goals in his last three games for Serie A side Frosinone.

Poland are forced to find an alternative option at left back after Przemyslaw Frankowski picked up an injury which is set to rule him out for the entire international break.

Piotr Zielinski and Marcel Regula both missed training after struggling with colds, but both will be a part of the squad in Bucharest.

Robert Lewandowski is expected to lead the attacking efforts, as he looks to add to his impressive tally of eight career goals against Romania - a run which includes successive hat-tricks against the Tricolour.

Hindrich; Bancu, Ilie, Dragusin, Ratiu; Dragomir, Ghita; Coman, Hagi, Man; Birligea

Dragowski; Puchacz, Kiwior, Potulski, Cash; Nowak; Zalewski, Zielinski, Szymanski, Swiderski; Lewandowski

Romania are in the midst of a turbulent time, but Poland’s run of three successive away defeats does not exude much confidence either.

This does not have the makings of a classic under the lights, and our prediction is a 1-1 draw.

#1588. Prickly Unai Emery fires back at 'more questions' from Sky Sports reporter in awkward interview after storming down Old Trafford tunnel before full time

By JAMES DUTTON, DEPUTY SPORTS NEWS EDITOR

Published: 16:35 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 17:09 EST, 8 November 2026

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery was in a prickly mood as he bit back at Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davison in a fiery end to his post-match interview at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Emery had just seen his Villa side twice throw away a two-goal lead against Manchester United – with Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scoring in stoppage time to secure a remarkable 4-4 draw.

The Villa boss was spotted storming down the touchline before the full-time whistle and after Dorgu's dramatic 97th-minute equaliser – with play continuing for another two minutes.

And the Villa boss, already exasperated at being asked 'more questions,' did not take kindly to being asked if he was emotional about the late equaliser or if he felt it was unfair.

When asked if his walking off was an emotional reaction, he responded: 'No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing.'

And then when asked whether the award of the goal was unfair, he replied: 'No, no. Not unfair. Please.

Unai Emery was in a prickly mood towards the end of his post match interview with Sky Sports

Emery had just stormed down the tunnel at Old Trafford after Aston Villa threw away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time

Emery took exception to being asked 'more questions' by Sky reporter Patrick Davison

'They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.'

Emery ended the interview making light of his 'poor' English, and then sarcastically asking if there were 'more questions' before an ironic 'Have a good Sunday' as he walked out of the interview.

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany complained on social media about the legitimacy of United's last-gasp equaliser.

He accused United goalkeeper Senne Lammens – who went up for the corner – of impeding his Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he looked to punch the ball clear.

After Roy Keane said 'football is a contact sport,' he posted on X: 'To put in context this convenient narrative of "contact sport" we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

'Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

'Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

'But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact.'

Michael Carrick was involved in a spiky interview with Sky Sports about his Man United future

Sky Sports' Davison's brush with Emery came just minutes after a spiky interview with beleaguered United boss Michael Carrick.

When the future of his own position was put to him by Davison, Carrick took exception to the question.

'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? You've been asked time and again about your future? I know you have said that you walking away was the best for the club, you'd probably do it,' Davison asked Carrick.

'It's not going to happen, no,' Carrick replied.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week. They conceded twice at the start of each half against Villa, and have now let in 30 goals in all competitions – the joint highest in Europe's top five leagues.

#1586. Liverpool transfer news: £85m Virgil van Dijk successor 'regularly' monitored ahead of summer but Real Madrid in picture

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 01:32, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 01:32

Liverpool have regularly monitored Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic ahead of the summer transfer window, the latest report has claimed.

The Reds have enjoyed a strong opening to the campaign, with the club fourth in the Premier League, and their only losses in the top flight have come against Arsenal and Manchester City.

Key to the upturn in form has been captain Virgil van Dijk, who has performed well in the heart of defence, helping his side keep four clean sheets.

However, the Dutchman's contract is set to expire at the end of 2026-27, and Andoni Iraola will need a replacement lined up if the 35-year-old leaves.

Journalist Florian Plettenberg has claimed that the Reds are looking closely at Brighton defender Vuskovic, who is valued at €100m (£85m), but the centre-back dreams of joining Real Madrid one day.

Brighton are second in the table with 22 points from a possible 30, and Vuskovic has arguably been the team's best player.

The Croatian is a strong passer, but he most importantly comes out on top in the majority of his individual battles, winning 60% of his duels in the league so far.

Vuskovic is often aggressive with his positioning, and that could make him the perfect partner Jeremy Jacquet, who is more comfortable in a reserved role.

The centre-back is only 19, so he would need time to adapt if he was to sign for the Reds, but he would be an incredible signing.

Van Dijk may still be among the best defenders in the Premier League, but Liverpool cannot continue to rely on the Dutchman forever.

Joe Gomez will likely depart this summer as well, while Ronald Araujo's loan deal from Barcelona may not be made permanent.

That would leave Giovanni Leoni and Jacquet as the only other senior centre-backs at the club, but they will be 20 and 22 respectively by the time next season starts.

While Vuskovic has been exceptional for Brighton, the Reds should consider signing at least two defenders in the summer transfer window in order to address concerns about their depth in defence.

With Matteo Gabbia sidelined until well into January and Fikayo Tomori currently injured, Amorim has been juggling an emergency in recent weeks. It was a situation further compounded by an issue that arose for Strahinja Pavlović last week.
